findings: All 17 required controls recompute consistently from score=min(1,G+A+F+R+C+T), with irreversible H overriding to zero, in contract order: 0.00, 0.20, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.30, 0.85, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 0.20, 0.20. Initial is 0; partial cases are 0.20, 0.30, and 0.85; full is 1.00; every specified hard failure is 0. R first becomes available after the fourth credited fracture. Timeout changes the inaccessible-fragment case by evaluating geometric inaccessibility and setting H before final scoring.

Timing is internally consistent: 7,200 controls at 20 Hz equals 360 s; production and refinement physics run at 240/480 Hz. The 300 s samples occur after POST(72000)/POST(144000), and timeout after POST(86400)/POST(172800). The initial diagnostic window, exact POST boundaries, settled-speed aggregation, penetration aggregation, and per-insert completed-strike interpretation are now explicit.

Contact freshness and aggregation are computable: PRE(n) supplies poses, twists, and joint state; POST(n) consumes only step-n contacts once; force is converted to impulse exactly once while native impulse is not rescaled; duplicate, stale, untagged, wrong-dt, and non-finite data set H. Repeated score/success reads cannot advance state.

Bad physical outcomes are preserved and scored as failures rather than conditionally suppressed. Native joint transitions occur before eligibility; invalid fracture, overload, glancing impact, direct hammer contact, insert/shell damage, forbidden penetration, fragment loss, unsafe self-contact, and timeout inaccessibility set H. Slow pressing, sequential one-arm operation, and other physically valid alternatives remain permitted and trigger reassessment if unexpectedly successful.

The two pinned runtime snapshots exist at permitted evidence locations and match the SHA256 values in the preflight index. Their provenance records identify the original paths and pinned IsaacLab commit. The PhysxManager snapshot confirms IsaacEvents PRE_PHYSICS_STEP/POST_PHYSICS_STEP registration, dt-bearing callbacks, returned CallbackHandle objects, native pre_step selection, and unsubscribe support. These facts support the prospective API design without claiming native validation.

The contract’s final approximation retains a historical statement that the snapshot directory was absent when the contract was authored. Current hash-verified snapshots resolve that lifecycle condition; the stale disclosure does not alter any task observable, formula, threshold, or required control and is not a remaining specification defect.

Industrial evidence supports four M2.5 × 3.75 mm shell-base inserts, tang removal, verification that tangs do not remain, fracture at the notch, and M2.5 mandrel 0158 040 1000. Unpublished geometry, forces, damage limits, and tolerances are explicitly identified as frozen prototype assumptions rather than industrial facts.

No material unresolved specification contradiction or ambiguous measurement remains. Native component behavior, timestep convergence, contact units/freshness, fracture dynamics, camera behavior, and demonstrations remain correctly deferred to later executed validation gates.
